key_insight: Large language models can extract semantic concepts from materials-science abstracts to build concept graphs whose temporal modeling predicts novel, high-potential combinations of research topics, surfacing ideas that inspire expert-driven new research.
problem_solved: As literature grows, finding promising, previously uncombined research directions is slow and biased; this work automates discovery by predicting emerging topic combinations from historical publication data.
method: Use LLMs to parse abstracts and extract semantic concepts and relations, creating a concept graph representation of the field.
Construct temporal snapshots of the concept graph and train a machine-learning predictor to forecast which concept combinations will emerge.
Present ranked candidate combinations to domain experts as interpretable suggestions to guide new research directions.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners and researchers with a scalable tool to surface promising, novel research hypotheses and prioritize exploration; demonstrates a practical LLM + graph-model pipeline for accelerating scientific discovery.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: abstracts → LLM extraction → concept graph → temporal predictor → suggested combinations
Evolving concept graph animation or series of snapshots showing new edges appearing over time
Timeline/heatmap of predicted emergence probabilities for topic pairs or clusters
Example card: specific suggested topic-combination with confidence score and expert annotation icon
paper_title: Predicting new research directions in materials science using large language models and concept graphs
paper_authors: Thomas Marwitz, Alexander Colsmann, Ben Breitung, Christoph Brabec, Christoph Kirchlechner
